comments.body:
## RCA evidence (2026-08-28, read-only investigation on i-00880b2c7f13527c5)

Confirms this ticket and localizes it precisely: **the app already serves the document; only the nginx edge fails to route it.**

Probed from the box, same moment:

    app  (direct, http://<container-ip>:8091)
      /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp   -> 200
      /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource       -> 404
      /mcp/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource   -> 404

    edge (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com)
      /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp   -> 404
      /mcp/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource   -> 404

401 challenge verbatim from the edge:

    www-authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token", error_description="Authentication required",
      resource_metadata="https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp"

### Mechanism

`infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template` declares only `location = /mcp/` (:157), `location = /mcp` (:178)
and the prefix `location /mcp` (:195) for the MCP app, plus `location /.well-known/acme-challenge/`
(:66). `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp` matches none of them, so it falls through to
`location /` (:224) -> `proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080` (Gerrit), which 404s. The live
`/etc/nginx/conf.d/rebar.conf` matches the template, so this reproduces on every deploy.

This narrows the ticket's AC#1: the fix is a one-location edge route, not a new server feature —
the resource-server metadata document exists and returns 200 on the app.

### Not the cause of the 2026-08-28 401 outage

Investigated alongside a live "MCP auth suddenly 401s" report. Independent: that report's root cause
was a client-side unexpanded `${MCP_CLIENT_PAT_COPILOT}` placeholder in `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`
(`rebar doctor` reports it as `copilot [error] pat-unresolvable`). Static-bearer clients never fetch
`resource_metadata`, and a probe with the real PAT returned `initialize` -> 200 while the edge
still 404s this path. So this stays P3, and it is not a client-recovery blocker today.

## Fix pushed for review — Gerrit change 2333

https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2333 (commit `8d72cbf414f4`, branch
`reb-71fe-wellknown-edge-route`). NOT submitted, NOT deployed; nginx on the box was not
reloaded.

### The change

`infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template` — one new exact-match location in the port-443 server
block, immediately before `location /`:

    location = /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp {
        proxy_pass http://rebar_mcp;
        ...forwarded headers + the same proxy_redirect http->https rules as the /mcp blocks
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Connection "";
    }

No URI path on `proxy_pass`, so the advertised URI reaches the app verbatim at the path it
already answers with 200. It names the `rebar_mcp` upstream rather than a port, so the
blue-green flip re-points it atomically. Exact match rather than a prefix, so it covers this
one document and cannot widen or reorder anything else under `/.well-known/`.

Nothing in the auth path, the 401 challenge text, or `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` was
touched.

### Regression tests (`tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py`, +75 lines)

Assert on the RENDERED config, not the raw template: a `_render_nginx()` helper substitutes
only `${REVIEW_BOT_PORT}`, and its output was confirmed byte-identical to
`REVIEW_BOT_PORT=8081 envsubst '${REVIEW_BOT_PORT}' < …`. Hermetic — no gettext binary
needed in CI.

- `test_nginx_routes_the_advertised_resource_metadata_url_to_the_mcp_app` — the exact-match
  location exists and proxies to `http://rebar_mcp` with no URI path.
- `test_nginx_metadata_route_does_not_shadow_the_acme_challenge` — the rendered config still
  serves the ACME challenge from `root /var/www/certbot;`.
- `test_nginx_template_substitutes_cleanly_under_envsubst` — no `${...}` survives rendering.

**Mutation check:** deleting the location block from the template turns
`test_nginx_routes_the_advertised_resource_metadata_url_to_the_mcp_app` RED (1 failed, 46
passed); restoring it returns 47 passed.

### Gates

`make lint` clean; `make typecheck` clean (683 files); `pytest
tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py` 4 passed; `check_complexity_baseline.py --check`
`active=39 new=0 increased=0 stale=10`. `tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py` 47 passed;
`tests/unit/test_opcert_deploy_infra.py` + `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_auth.py` 38
passed.

### Scope note

Reiterating the RCA: this is a correctness/standards fix, not the cause of any client-auth
failure. Static-bearer clients never fetch `resource_metadata`. Live edge fetchability
becomes observable only after the change lands and deploys.

## Closing — change 2333 merged; AC verification

Gerrit change 2333 landed on `main` as commit `b75bf4bc0951` ("Route the OAuth metadata URL at
the edge"), touching exactly the two declared `file_impact` paths and nothing else. It is the
ONLY code commit referencing this ticket (`git log --all --grep=71fe-2579-28cc-409c` returns it
plus its pre-submit patchset `8d72cbf414f4` and the tracker's own event commits), so the recorded
`file_impact` needed no widening.

### AC-by-AC

- **AC1 — edge routes the advertised URL to the MCP app.** MET. `infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template`
  now carries `location = /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp` in the 443 server block with
  `proxy_pass http://rebar_mcp;` and no URI path, placed after the `/mcp` locations and before
  `location /`. `test_nginx_routes_the_advertised_resource_metadata_url_to_the_mcp_app` asserts it
  against the RENDERED config.
- **AC2 — a check fails if the advertised URL is not routable at the edge.** MET as the AC scopes
  it: the AC's own text names the rendering test as the in-session observable proxy and puts live
  fetchability out of scope ("only observable after a deploy"). That test is present and passing.
  **Live status recorded honestly, not ticked:** probed just now,
  `GET https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp` still
  returns **404 ("Not Found")**. The merge has not been deployed — nginx on the box has not been
  reloaded with the new config, and this ticket deliberately excludes the deploy. The live route
  will only answer 200 after the next deploy picks up `b75bf4bc0951`.
- **AC3 — no ACME/MCP regression.** MET. The rendered config still carries
  `location /.well-known/acme-challenge/` with `root /var/www/certbot;`
  (`test_nginx_metadata_route_does_not_shadow_the_acme_challenge`), and the full
  `tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py` suite is **47 passed** on the merged tree.
- **AC4 — gates green.** MET at push time (recorded in the previous comment) and re-confirmed by
  the merged change carrying `Verified +1` before Submit.

### Residual, deliberately not blocking this close

Live edge fetchability depends on a deploy, which is out of scope here. If the next deploy does
not clear the 404, that is a deploy-pipeline observation, not a defect in this fix.

compiled_state.description:
## Summary

The MCP endpoint's `401` challenge advertises a protected-resource metadata URL that does not
exist at the edge.

    www-authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token", ...
      resource_metadata="https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp"

    GET https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp -> 404

## Context / Problem

RFC 9728 metadata discovery is how an OAuth-capable client learns where to authenticate. A
client that follows the advertised URL gets a 404 and cannot discover the resource server.

Today's clients use STATIC bearer PATs and do not consult it, so nothing is currently broken in
practice — which is why this is P3 rather than higher. It matters if/when OAuth clients are
enabled, and an advertised-but-missing URL is misleading regardless.

## Pre-existing, not caused by the HTTPS-downgrade fix

Confirmed against the pre-change backup of `/etc/nginx/conf.d/rebar.conf`: there is no such
location block BEFORE or AFTER that deploy. The nginx config has never served the path.

## Root cause (confirmed, see the RCA comment)

The application already serves the document — probed from the box, the app direct on
`127.0.0.1:8091` returns `200` for `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp` while the edge
returns `404`. `infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template` declares only `location = /mcp/`, `location =
/mcp`, the prefix `location /mcp`, and `location /.well-known/acme-challenge/`. The advertised
path matches none of them, so it falls through to `location /` -> `proxy_pass
http://127.0.0.1:8080` (Gerrit), which 404s.

## Approach

Add ONE exact-match nginx location for the advertised path to the port-443 server block in
`infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template`, proxying to the existing named upstream with NO URI path on
`proxy_pass`, so the request URI reaches the app verbatim — exactly the path the app already
answers with 200.

Why this approach fits: the defect is purely a missing edge route (the app half already works),
so the narrowest correct fix is one routing rule and nothing else. `location =` (exact match)
is used rather than a prefix so it cannot widen `/.well-known/` beyond this single document and
cannot shadow the existing `location /.well-known/acme-challenge/` used by certbot. The
upstream is named — `upstream rebar_mcp { include /etc/nginx/mcp-upstream*.conf; }` at
`infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template:56-58` — so the new block reuses `proxy_pass
http://rebar_mcp;` and inherits the blue-green atomic flip instead of hardcoding a port. The
block carries the same forwarded headers and `proxy_redirect` http->https upgrade rules the
existing MCP blocks carry (`infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template:157,178,195`), because an
exact-match location inherits nothing from the prefix location.

This is a correctness/standards fix, not an outage fix. It deliberately does NOT touch the
authentication path, the 401 challenge text, or `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`.

## Scope

- `infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template` — new `location = /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp`
  in the 443 server block, before `location /`.
- `tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py` — regression test, alongside the existing nginx
  contract tests (`test_nginx_mcp_location_proxies_to_the_named_upstream` at line 156 and
  `test_nginx_serves_the_documented_mcp_slash_url_without_redirecting` at line 834).

## Testing

- Happy path: the RENDERED config (the template passed through `envsubst '${REVIEW_BOT_PORT}'`,
  the exact substitution documented at `infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template:5-12`) contains an
  exact-match `location = /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp` whose body is
  `proxy_pass http://rebar_mcp;` with no URI path, so the advertised URI is preserved.
- Edge: the same rendered output still contains `location /.well-known/acme-challenge/` with
  its `root /var/www/certbot;`, proving the new exact-match block does not shadow ACME
  issuance/renewal; and the rendered text contains no unsubstituted `${` sequence, proving the
  new block introduced nothing envsubst would eat.
- Mutation check: deleting the new location block from the template must turn the new test RED.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The edge routes the advertised metadata URL to the MCP app instead of falling through to
      Gerrit: the rendered nginx config contains an exact-match
      `location = /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp` proxying to `http://rebar_mcp`
      with no URI path; verified by a new test in `tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py` that
      renders the template and asserts the block, and that fails when the block is removed.
- [x] A check fails if the advertised `resource_metadata` URL is not routable at the edge:
      the same new test is the in-session observable proxy — it renders the template and fails
      if no location matches the advertised path (live fetchability is only observable after a
      deploy, which is out of scope for this ticket).
- [x] The new block does not regress ACME or MCP routing: the rendered config still carries
      `location /.well-known/acme-challenge/` with `root /var/www/certbot;`, and the existing
      nginx tests in `tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py` still pass.
- [x] Gates are green: `make lint`, `make typecheck`,
      `pytest tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py`, and
      `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` all exit 0.

file_impact.reason: add the exact-match edge route for /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp to the named MCP upstream
regression test asserting the rendered config routes the advertised resource_metadata URL
